title: Tevilat Kelim - Dipping Before Selling or Gifting (1)

chapters.title: Introduction to Tevilat Kelim for Gifts and Sales
chapters.about: A bride dipping gifts for friends and store owners dipping utensils for customers.

chapters.title: Gemara Sources for Tevilat Kelim
chapters.about: Exploring Masechet Abodah Zarah and the derivation from the word v'tahar.

chapters.title: New Utensils and Kele Seuda
chapters.about: Whether brand new utensils require immersion and the limitation to food utensils.

chapters.title: Borrowing vs. Purchasing from a Non-Jew
chapters.about: Tosafot, Rashbam, and Hagahot Ashiri on borrowed utensils and different intentions.

chapters.title: Taz and Yisur VeHeter on Intentions
chapters.about: Analyzing whether changing the purpose of a utensil creates an obligation for immersion.

chapters.title: Pri Hadash and Chacham Ovadia Yosef
chapters.about: Majority usage, store owners immersing items, and practical halakhic conclusions.

summary: Rabbi Harari discusses the halakhic status of performing Tevilat Kelim on utensils when the person who immerses them is not currently obligated, such as a shopkeeper selling utensils or someone buying them as a gift. He explores various opinions among the Rishonim and Acharonim, including Beit Yosef, Taz, and Pri Hadash, regarding whether such immersion is effective or if the final owner must immerse them again. The class examines the legal mechanics and parallels from other areas of halakha like Berachot HaTorah and Tefillin.
questions: Can a store owner immerse new metal or glass utensils before selling them to a customer?
If someone buys a utensil as a gift and immerses it beforehand, does the recipient need to immerse it again?
Does a utensil require Tevilat Kelim if the Jewish owner initially bought it from a non-Jew for non-food purposes, like cutting parchment?
What is the difference between borrowing a utensil from a non-Jew versus buying it through a Jewish middleman regarding Tevilat Kelim?
